question: Who are the first order intestate successors in Estonia and how do children share the estate?
reference: Under the Estonian Law of Succession Act (§ 13) the first order intestate successors are the descendants of the bequeather. Children succeed in equal shares, and a descendant who died before the bequeather is replaced by his or her own descendants, who share that part equally.

question: What share of the estate does a surviving spouse receive in Estonia when there is no will?
reference: Under § 16 of the Estonian Law of Succession Act the surviving spouse inherits together with the relatives: with first order successors (descendants) the spouse receives a share equal to that of a child but not less than one quarter of the estate; with second order successors one half of the estate; if there are no first or second order relatives the spouse receives the entire estate.

question: How large is the compulsory portion in Estonia?
reference: Under § 105 of the Estonian Law of Succession Act the compulsory portion is one half of the value of the share of the estate that the successor would have received in intestate succession if all intestate successors had accepted the succession. If the person has been left less than the compulsory portion, he or she may claim the missing part from the co-successors.

question: In Estonia, what belongs to the joint property of spouses and what is separate property?
reference: Under the Estonian Family Law Act, in the regime of jointness of property the objects and proprietary rights acquired by the spouses during the jointness become their joint property (§ 25). Separate property is excluded from it (§ 27): personal effects, objects owned before the marriage or acquired during the marriage without charge (gift or succession), objects acquired on the basis of or as compensation for separate property, and mandatory pension fund units.

question: How is joint property divided between spouses in Estonia when the jointness of property ends?
reference: Under § 37 of the Estonian Family Law Act, after the termination of jointness of property the spouses divide the joint property between themselves in equal parts, unless otherwise agreed. The composition of joint property is determined as of the termination of the proprietary relationship, and the application for division can be submitted to court together with the divorce action.

question: What form must a marital property contract have in Estonia?
reference: Under § 60 of the Estonian Family Law Act a marital property contract must be entered into by the spouses in person and in notarially authenticated form.

question: In Estonia, when is a divorce granted by a court instead of a vital statistics office?
reference: Under § 64 of the Estonian Family Law Act a vital statistics office or a notary may grant a divorce on a joint written petition when the spouses agree and Estonian law applies. Under § 65 a court grants the divorce on the action of one spouse when the spouses disagree about the divorce or its circumstances, or when the vital statistics office or notary is not competent.

question: Who are the forced heirs under Slovenian law?
reference: Under Article 25 of the Slovenian Inheritance Act forced heirs are the deceased's descendants, adoptive children and their descendants, the parents and the spouse. Grandparents and brothers and sisters are forced heirs only if they are permanently incapacitated for work and lack the necessary means of subsistence, and all of them only when entitled to inherit under the law of succession.

question: How large is the statutory portion of a child in Slovenia?
reference: Under Article 26 of the Slovenian Inheritance Act the statutory portion of descendants, adoptive children and their descendants, and of the spouse is one half of the share they would receive under intestate succession; for the other forced heirs it is one third. The rest of the estate is the disposable portion.

question: Is a handwritten will without a date valid in Slovenia?
reference: Yes. Under Article 63 of the Slovenian Inheritance Act a will handwritten and signed by the testator is valid, even when it does not state the date on which it was written.

question: How can a will be made in front of witnesses in Slovenia?
reference: Under Article 64 of the Slovenian Inheritance Act a testator who can read and write may sign in his or her own hand, in front of two witnesses, a document drawn up by another person, declaring in front of them that it is his or her will. The two witnesses sign the will; the postscript that they sign as witnesses is not a condition of validity.

question: Who inherits first in Slovenia when there is no will?
reference: Under Article 11 of the Slovenian Inheritance Act the estate is inherited first and foremost by the deceased's children and spouse, who inherit equal portions.

question: What is co-owned property of spouses in Slovenia?
reference: Under Article 67 of the Slovenian Family Code co-owned property is all property rights acquired by work or against payment during the marriage, and property acquired on the basis of co-owned property. Under Article 68 it belongs jointly to both spouses, their shares are not specified, and a spouse cannot dispose of or encumber his or her unspecified share by transactions inter vivos.

question: What is the separate property of a spouse in Slovenia?
reference: Under Article 77 of the Slovenian Family Code separate property is property acquired before the marriage or received without consideration during the marriage; items of small value intended for exclusively personal use are also separate property.

question: Who are the legitimaries (forced heirs) in Italy?
reference: Under Article 536 of the Italian Civil Code the persons for whom the law reserves a share of the inheritance are the spouse, the children and the ascendants. Adopted children are equated with children, and descendants who come to the succession in place of a child have the same rights.

question: What share of the estate is reserved to the children in Italy when there is no spouse?
reference: Under Article 537 of the Italian Civil Code, if the parent leaves a single child, one half of the estate is reserved to the child; if there are more children, two thirds are reserved to them, divided equally (Article 542 applies when there is also a spouse).

question: What are the requirements of a holographic will in Italy?
reference: Under Article 602 of the Italian Civil Code a holographic will must be written in full, dated and signed by the hand of the testator. The signature must be at the end of the provisions and is valid even without first and last name if it identifies the testator with certainty; the date must indicate day, month and year. Article 601 lists the holographic will and the notarial will as the ordinary forms.

question: In Italian intestate succession, what share does the spouse receive together with children?
reference: Under Article 581 of the Italian Civil Code, when the spouse concurs with children the spouse is entitled to one half of the estate if there is only one child, and to one third in the other cases.

question: Which assets fall into the community of property of spouses in Italy?
reference: Under Article 177 of the Italian Civil Code the community includes: property acquired by the spouses together or separately during the marriage (except personal property); the fruits of each spouse's property received and not consumed at the dissolution; the proceeds of each spouse's activity still existing at the dissolution; companies managed by both spouses and established after the marriage (for companies owned by one spouse before the marriage but managed by both, only profits and increases).

question: Which assets remain personal property of a spouse in Italy?
reference: Under Article 179 of the Italian Civil Code personal property includes: property owned before the marriage; property acquired by gift or inheritance (unless allocated to the community); property for strictly personal use; property used for the spouse's profession; damages and pensions for loss of working capacity; property acquired with the price of personal property.

question: When is the community of property between spouses dissolved in Italy?
reference: Under Article 191 of the Italian Civil Code the community is dissolved by declaration of absence or presumed death of a spouse, annulment, dissolution or termination of the civil effects of the marriage, legal separation, judicial separation of property, conventional change of the property regime and bankruptcy of a spouse. In legal separation it is dissolved when the court president authorises the spouses to live separately or when the minutes of the consensual separation are signed.

question: Compare the reserved share of children in Italy and Slovenia.
reference: In Italy (Art. 537) one half of the estate is reserved to a single child and two thirds to two or more children; with a surviving spouse (Art. 542) one child receives one third and several children one half in total. In Slovenia (Art. 26 Inheritance Act) the statutory portion of descendants is one half of the share they would receive under intestate succession; the rest is the disposable portion. Italy uses fixed fractions of the whole estate, Slovenia a fraction of each heir's intestate share.

question: Compare the intestate share of a surviving spouse who inherits together with children in Estonia and Slovenia.
reference: In Estonia (§ 16 Law of Succession Act) the spouse inheriting with descendants receives a share equal to that of a child but not less than one quarter of the estate. In Slovenia (Art. 11 Inheritance Act) the children and the spouse inherit first and in equal portions; there is no minimum quarter.

question: Compare what counts as separate (personal) property of a spouse in Italy, Estonia and Slovenia.
reference: In all three countries property owned before the marriage and property received for free during the marriage (gifts, inheritance) stays separate. Italy (Art. 179) also lists property for strictly personal use, property used for the profession and damages or pensions for loss of working capacity. Estonia (§ 27) adds personal effects, objects acquired with or as compensation for separate property and mandatory pension fund units. Slovenia (Art. 77) adds items of small value for exclusively personal use.

question: Is the common property of spouses divided equally in Italy and in Estonia?
reference: Yes in both. In Italy (Art. 194) the assets and liabilities of the community are divided in equal parts, and the judge may grant one spouse the usufruct of part of the other's share for the needs of the children. In Estonia (§ 37) joint property is divided into equal parts unless the spouses agree otherwise.

question: Who has a right to a reserved or compulsory share of the estate in Italy, Estonia and Slovenia?
reference: Italy (Art. 536): spouse, children (adopted children included) and ascendants. Slovenia (Art. 25): descendants, adoptive children and their descendants, parents and spouse; grandparents and siblings only if unable to work and without means. Estonia (§ 104): descendants, parents and spouse who would inherit in intestacy and to whom the bequeather owed maintenance can claim a compulsory portion if disinherited or given less.

question: Describe an Italian inheritance case solved by mediation in Nola: how long did it take and how was it resolved?
reference: In case 426/2019 an inheritance dispute between a spouse, children and other relatives lasted about 360 days and ended with a conciliatory agreement at a mediation meeting in Nola on 29 July 2019: one heir transferred three properties in Nola to the mother and another property to the sister, with a compensation of about 3,757.60 euro, and the other heir did not oppose.

question: Find an Estonian case on the division of joint property, loans and bank accounts after a divorce. What happened?
reference: In Estonian case 2-12-44594 the former spouses disputed the division of joint property, loans and bank accounts after the divorce. The defendant appealed; the district court found that the county court had violated procedural rules (it ignored the request to question witnesses) and ordered a new review. The parties finally reached a compromise agreement; the case lasted about 8 years.

question: Find an Estonian inheritance case where a counterclaim asked to end the joint ownership of the succession assets and divide them equally.
reference: In Estonian case 2-16-18628 one party sued over the division of succession assets and the other filed a counterclaim to terminate joint ownership and divide them equally. The court partially satisfied the counterclaim, ordered the division of the assets and gave half of the estate (471,972 euro) to the counterclaimant, also recognising a claim for funeral expenses; the case lasted about 6 years and 8 months and each party bore its own costs.

question: Find a Slovenian appeal decision about an estate that included an unpaid pension.
reference: In Slovenian case VSL sklep I Cp 1461/2016 the court of appeal rejected the appeal and confirmed the first instance decision. The estate included an unpaid pension and was divided among the heirs, with heir BB receiving half; Mr AA claimed a share of the proceeds of an apartment sale but was found to have no standing to assert his rights in the succession proceedings.

question: How long do Italian court cases on the division of an estate last?
reference: Italian court cases on the division of an estate usually last several years: in the past cases of the dataset durations range from about 7 years (case 6009/2013) to around 9 years (Tribunale di Bari 2672/2022) and more than 10 years in other cases; they depend on the complexity of the estate and the number of heirs.

question: Chi sono i legittimari secondo il codice civile italiano?
reference: Secondo l'articolo 536 del codice civile italiano i legittimari, cioè le persone a cui la legge riserva una quota dell'eredità, sono il coniuge, i figli e gli ascendenti; i figli adottivi sono equiparati ai figli e i discendenti che subentrano al posto di un figlio hanno gli stessi diritti.

question: Quanto spetta al coniuge superstite in Estonia se ci sono figli e non c'è testamento?
reference: Secondo il § 16 della legge estone sulle successioni il coniuge superstite che eredita insieme ai discendenti riceve una quota pari a quella di un figlio, ma non inferiore a un quarto dell'eredità.

question: In Slovenia un testamento scritto a mano senza data è valido?
reference: Sì. Secondo l'articolo 63 della legge slovena sulle successioni il testamento scritto a mano e firmato dal testatore è valido anche se non indica la data in cui è stato scritto.

question: What is a will?
reference: A will is a legal document in which a person (the testator) states how his or her property is to be distributed after death; it can name heirs and legatees and must respect the formal requirements of the law.

question: What does intestate succession mean in general?
reference: Intestate succession is the transfer of a deceased person's estate according to the rules of law, which apply when the person left no valid will (or the will covers only part of the estate); the law then determines the heirs and their shares, usually by degree of kinship and with the surviving spouse.

question: What is the penalty for theft in Italy?
reference: Theft in Italy is a crime under the Italian Criminal Code, punished with imprisonment and a fine, with higher penalties for aggravated theft.
